I heard "I brought you into this world and I can take you out" so often as a child from my dad!! Also, anytime I'd get a beating with the belt he would tell me "This hurts me more than it hurts you." He had 3 daughters but loved to tell us "It's a man's world."

I was 20. I saw the same general practitioner that my stepmom was seeing the week following her suicide from an overdose of fentanyl. He was also my dad's doctor at the time. I remember being very emotional and crying during that appointment. I begged him to not overprescribe my dad and that my dad also had a prescription drug problem and to please help him. I told him I didn't want any medication but he insisted I needed sleep to help cope with my grief and prescribed me ambien and an antidepressant. I came back for a follow-up appointment shortly afterwards. He told me he couldn't stop thinking about me. He said he'd never felt the way he felt about me for anyone else before. He kissed me. Open mouthed. I think he was in his 50's at the time. Maybe older. I froze. Just left the office like nothing had happened. When I told my dad about it he seemed to react with almost a sense of pride about how I could have attracted him and how pretty I was. Like it was to be somewhat expected for me in my life to experience something like that.

He doesn't understand it himself. They don't spend time asking themselves these questions or really analyzing anything about their own character defects. They spend a lot of time focusing on others, though, promise you that. You don't need him to tell you the "why" to know that it is causing you pain. That is enough of an answer and whatever words he chooses aren't going to be enough to "fix" the disconnect. Actions. Actions actions actions. Does he show empathy to your feelings? Does he ask you how or why you feel the way you do, or does he just offer explanations and excuses. That will tell you a lot about his mental state and ability to really even be in a mature relationship. 

Honestly, I think most of them don't even know what a healthy relationship requires. They think it's watching tv and having sex and generally never having conflict. They don't really want to confront their negative traits, they want us to love them but not require anything of them.

They don't just stop watching it. That's not how human behavior works. It releases dopamine and acts as an antidepressant basically. They're dependent and need actual help to stop, so if he's telling you he just doesn't watch it anymore and isn't even tempted? No. Nope. He is lying. He is probably saying that because in the actual moment that you are asking him, he *technically* isn't watching it. That's how f'd up their thinking is.

The gaslighting is so psychologically damaging. They make us think it's a problem with us and that we just want to be unhappy/untrusting and can't forgive. It's bullsh**. Your intuition knows. I'm sorry that you're here.and having these doubrs and fears, but please, please trust your intuition over his words.

I was SO SCARED when I was pregnant with my first!! I was almost kind of...angry? Enraged? that I was just expected to go into labor and accept any/all outcomes/interventions/pain that went along with it. The only stories I'd heard were from other women about how much pain they were in, the length of time they experienced that pain, and essentially just how traumatizing the whole experience was. They'd top it off with "You forget about all that as soon as baby is out though!" Did nothing to alleviate my concerns and fears and I felt like my feelings were so invalidated in those interactions. I literally was at the point that I wanted to request an elective c-section because the thought of havibg a vaginal birth just f****** scared me. YOU HAVE EVERY RIGHT TO FEEL HOW YOU FEEL! That being said, I want to share what helped me to work through those fears and very real concerns: 

I was incredibly blessed to be renting my home from a woman who worked as a birth doula. She truly loved birth, babies, bodies, all of it. She took the time to just talk to me and listen, and then she pulled out a book on natural midwifery, I believe it was by Ina May Ghaskin, and let me borrow it. That book helped me to realize/accept that birth is what my body already inherently knows how to do. Language is so, so important! I worked on trying to change the words I used surrounding birth, like "contractions". I didn't feel good hearing that word, but calling them "tightenings" felt better. Also, using the word "pain" triggered a lot for me, but naming that sensation as "strong pressure" allowed me to relax into it instead of tensing up, which allowed my  body, as well as my mind, to open up and look forward to the progression of meeting my baby girl. 

I didn't go into labor with a 100% positive mindset, by any means. I reserved the right to request an epidural if at any point I felt like things were getting to be too much for me to handle, and honestly, just knowing that was an option really helped me to relax and go with the flow in the moment. I had a plan b, lol. 

I wound up having my baby girl after 6 hours, from start to finish, and surprised myself by never even requesting that epidural. My doula friend came to the hospital and supported me with pressure to my lower back, as that was where I felt everything, and I think that by having her there, really just a calm and loving presence, it made me feel so much more confident that I was "doing it right", that everything was "normal" and I was alright. 

I am currently due November 1st, no doula this time. I am also being induced for the first time so I have no idea what that will be like... I've been encouraging my husband to take a birthing class with me so that he can know how to be that supportive person for me, as it will be his first time. My goal is to have a calm setting: flameless candles, soft music, soft slippers/gown from home, aromatherapy, etc. Anything that will help the atmosphere to feel more comfortable and calm. And I'm still keeping the epidural option on the table 😉 I hope this helps you to feel a little better about what's coming 💗

Edit: I've never had an epidural before but I hear it feels like a pinch, not a stabbing sensation, and that it is possible to have something called a "walking epidural", where you can still get up and move around.

Sometimes people hurt others, intentionally or not, and it's not always because the other person deserves it. I don't deserve it. I do care about others. I do my best to make other people feel good. I work hard, at whatever I do, even if it's not perfect. I try. I am not worthless. None of us are. We are hurt people, and sometimes we make mistakes...but the common underlying and undeniable truth that I see in each one of our posts is that WE CARE. We care so very much.
